L30-L55 the IntersectionObserver useEffect is ported to the working `useSectionAnchors` hook. L31 `if (chips.length === 0) return` -> the hook tolerates an empty chip list (loops produce no match, activeId stays ''). L33-L47 `new IntersectionObserver(..., { rootMargin: '-${topOffset + 80}px 0px -60% 0px', threshold: 0 })` -> the hook's `onScroll` derives the active chip from the live scroll offset using the SAME activation line: `scrollY + topOffset + 80` (ACTIVE_LINE_OFFSET = 80, mirroring the rootMargin top inset). L35-L40 'topmost intersecting entry wins' (`reduce` to smallest boundingClientRect.top, `setActiveId(top.target.id)`) -> the native scrollspy picks the section with the greatest registered offsetY that is still <= the activation line (the topmost section past the line), then `setActiveId`. L49-L52 `chips.forEach(chip => document.getElementById(chip.id); observer.observe(el))` -> sections register their vertical offset through `registerSection(id)` wired to each section's `onLayout`. L54 `return () => observer.disconnect()` -> no global observer to disconnect; the handler lifetime is owned by the host ScrollView (parity with ScrollRestoration). L55 deps `[chips, topOffset]` honoured by the hook's `onScroll` deps.

L57-L75 `handleClick(id)` ported two ways. The bar's `handlePress` (uncontrolled) preserves `setActiveId(id)` (L74) and calls `onChipPress`. The full scroll math lives in the hook's `scrollToSection`: L58-L59 `document.getElementById(id); if (!el) return` -> `offsets.current.get(id)` with an early return when the section has not registered. L60 `navRef.current?.offsetHeight ?? 0` -> dropped (native bar does not overlap the content). L70-L73 the `window.scrollTo` fallback has no native analogue (window.scrollY is always 0 on web anyway) and is documented in stickyChipBarCapabilities. L74 `setActiveId(id)` preserved (scrollToSection marks active immediately, like the web click). L75 deps `[topOffset]` honoured (scrollToSection deps include topOffset/scrollPadding/scrollRef).

The whole file is a single status component (no further exports in the source); the port additionally exposes `useSectionAnchors` + `SectionAnchorsApi`/`UseSectionAnchorsOptions` (the working native replacement for the browser-only observer + DOM scroll) and `stickyChipBarCapabilities` (explicit unavailable-state record per parity-contract rule 7).

Native-safe adaptations summary: IntersectionObserver -> useSectionAnchors scrollspy off the host ScrollView offset using the identical `topOffset + 80` activation line; document.getElementById + scrollEl.scrollTo({behavior:'smooth'}) + window.scrollTo fallback -> registerSection(onLayout) + scrollToSection(scrollRef.scrollTo); navRef.offsetHeight subtraction -> dropped (bar is above, not overlapping, the content); cn/clsx/tailwind-merge -> StyleSheet style arrays; position:sticky/z-index/backdrop-blur -> fixed header + translucent fill; web scrollbar styling -> hidden native indicator; CSS variables (--bg-1, --surface-2, --text-secondary) + cyan-400/cyan-200 Tailwind stops -> mirrored colour constants. The source uses no react-i18next, so no i18n is fabricated; the only literal ('Jump to section') is preserved exactly as the accessibilityLabel. No DOM, IntersectionObserver, recharts, leaflet, or web UI components are imported -- only React Native primitives and the existing native AppText component.
